principle: Developer ownership and control is the default (IC-175, IC-176). Krate enforces a boundary only where portability, the recipient's permission, OS safety, evidence, the platform, or the law requires it; everything else is the application's choice, and for every enforced boundary a lower-level portable interface is named or its absence is recorded as a gap.

justifications.portability: the same file must run on every host Krate supports, so the shape every host lowers to is fixed
justifications.recipient-permission: the person running the app decides what it may reach; the boundary is where they decide
justifications.os-safety: the host, the person's other data and other apps must not be reachable by an app that was not granted them
justifications.evidence: a claim about the app must rest on something a check can read
justifications.platform: the operating system offers this one way, and Krate cannot offer another
justifications.legal: a law or a licence requires it

boundaries.standardizes: the sample formats and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what the app does with the samples
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the device boundary: opening an output is a grant the person gives
boundaries.application_choice: synthesis, mixing, codecs and formats; the app decodes with any library it likes and hands over PCM
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw PCM buffers -- no codec or mixer of Krate's is between the app and the device

boundaries.standardizes: how much of a stream is still waiting to be heard, so a stream can stay on time
boundaries.application_choice: how far ahead it writes
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: it reads a number and grants nothing new

boundaries.standardizes: the microphone boundary: opening an input is a grant the person gives
boundaries.application_choice: what is done with the audio: recognition, recording, analysis, by any library
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw PCM frames

boundaries.standardizes: frame and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what the app does with a frame
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the camera boundary: opening a camera is a grant the person gives
boundaries.application_choice: frame processing, encoding, vision, by any library
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw frames, pulled at the app's own rate

boundaries.standardizes: path, mode and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what the app does with a file
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the filesystem boundary: paths are sandbox-relative, reachable only under a grant the person gave, and never resolve outside it
boundaries.application_choice: file formats, parsers, layouts on disk, any library over the bytes
boundaries.escape_hatch: the file picker (ui/dialog) for a path outside the grants, chosen by the person; store.* for the app's own data with no grant at all

boundaries.standardizes: that a watch sees only what listing the folder could: same path rules, same grant check on every look, a bounded tree and at most four looks a second
boundaries.application_choice: which folders, how often to ask, and what a change means
boundaries.escape_hatch: list and stat the folder itself on the app's own schedule

boundaries.standardizes: colour, rectangle and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: everything drawn with them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the handoff of drawn pixels and draw operations to the host painter, which is the only way onto the screen
boundaries.application_choice: any rasterizer, layout engine, text shaper or scene graph the app brings; Krate's draw calls are a convenience, not a requirement
boundaries.escape_hatch: set-pixels on a canvas or an image widget: the app renders with anything and hands over the pixels
boundaries.gap: a developer's own GPU renderer goes through krate:gpu, which presents by copying each frame into the canvas through the CPU until the presenter shares its device (K-407); scene3d is software

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: an optional software 3D helper
boundaries.application_choice: any 3D approach; the app may ignore this entirely
boundaries.escape_hatch: canvas pixels from the app's own renderer

boundaries.standardizes: WebGPU's descriptor, command and error shapes, with formats, features and limits by their WebGPU names
boundaries.application_choice: every resource, shader, pipeline and pass the app makes from them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: WebGPU's object model over host handles: shaders are WGSL validated by the host before any driver sees them, every call returns its own error, and a surface presents into a canvas widget
boundaries.application_choice: any renderer or engine: its own buffers, textures, pipelines, WGSL shaders, render and compute passes, frame pacing and post-processing
boundaries.escape_hatch: canvas pixels from the app's own software renderer

boundaries.standardizes: IO record and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what the app does with them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the byte-stream resource stdio and future IO surfaces share
boundaries.application_choice: framing, encoding, protocols over the bytes
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw bytes

boundaries.standardizes: that a CLI app's standard streams are the host process's
boundaries.application_choice: what is written and read, in any format
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw bytes on streams

boundaries.standardizes: how launch arguments reach the app
boundaries.application_choice: parsing and meaning of the arguments
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw strings

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: an optional structured log the host can show
boundaries.application_choice: any logging scheme, or stderr
boundaries.escape_hatch: stdio

boundaries.standardizes: locale and formatting type shapes
boundaries.application_choice: what is done with them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: how the person's locale and timezone are read from the host
boundaries.application_choice: whether to honour them
boundaries.escape_hatch: ignore the host and let the person choose in the app

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: optional host-backed formatting
boundaries.application_choice: any formatting library shipped in the app
boundaries.escape_hatch: format in the app

boundaries.standardizes: request, response and error shapes every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what is sent and how it is interpreted
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: the network boundary: a request reaches only a host the person granted, and the host and port are checked before anything dials
boundaries.application_choice: which servers, which APIs, which protocols over HTTP, how redirects and retries are handled (the client follows nothing on its own)
boundaries.escape_hatch: the request and response are raw bytes and headers; any protocol over HTTP is the app's

boundaries.standardizes: the same boundary for a live connection: a net.connect grant to that host and port, checked at open
boundaries.application_choice: the protocol over the socket, the framing, the server
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw message frames; krate:net/sockets for a transport of the app's own

boundaries.standardizes: the same net.connect boundary at the lowest level: every TCP connection and every UDP datagram's destination is judged against the person's grants before any socket exists; an address stands only for the names the app's own lookups resolved to it; a UDP socket hears only addresses it sent to
boundaries.application_choice: the protocol, the framing, the client library (std-like types, tokio and quinn adapters in net-krate; QUIC runs over it)
boundaries.escape_hatch: raw bytes and datagrams
boundaries.gap: listening for incoming connections is not offered yet, so an app cannot host a server (IC-935)

boundaries.standardizes: the first-generation host world, kept for the bundles that use it
boundaries.application_choice: none new: this world is superseded and not for new apps
boundaries.escape_hatch: the Phase 2 and Phase 3 worlds

boundaries.standardizes: that a program runs only when the manifest names it by its bare name and the person allowed it, is found on the person's PATH or in ~/.cargo/bin without the app learning where, runs in the app's own folder or one the person picked, gets the person's environment without Krate's, and ends with the app, its whole process group with it
boundaries.application_choice: which programs, their arguments and input, how output is read and shown, whether to offer a terminal
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a program is the person's own tool, and not running one costs the app nothing else

boundaries.standardizes: where operating-system randomness comes from
boundaries.application_choice: any PRNG or crate over it (rand, uuid, getrandom route here)
boundaries.escape_hatch: seed the app's own generator from it, or use none

boundaries.standardizes: that the app's own bundled files are readable with no grant, because they are the app's
boundaries.application_choice: what is bundled and in what format
boundaries.escape_hatch: embed bytes in the component itself

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: an optional local recogniser over audio the app already holds
boundaries.application_choice: any model or recogniser shipped in assets, or a service the app calls itself over the network boundary
boundaries.escape_hatch: audio/capture frames processed by the app
boundaries.gap: the recogniser reads one model family; another engine means the app ships its own

boundaries.standardizes: that speech is sound: allowed by audio.playback, replaced rather than queued, and stopped when the app stops
boundaries.application_choice: what is said, when, in which of the computer's voices and at what speed
boundaries.escape_hatch: audio/playback with the app's own synthesizer or recorded clips

boundaries.standardizes: that an app's own data lives in a namespace derived from its verified lineage, so a file claiming the same id cannot read it
boundaries.application_choice: whether to use it at all; any data model over it
boundaries.escape_hatch: fs/files under a grant with the app's own storage library, or the app's own format inside the bundle

boundaries.standardizes: the same namespace rule for a database
boundaries.application_choice: schema, queries, whether to use SQL at all; any embedded database over fs/files under a grant
boundaries.escape_hatch: fs/files with the app's own database library

boundaries.standardizes: that a secret is encrypted at rest under the app's own key and never lands beside the person's documents
boundaries.application_choice: what is stored and for how long
boundaries.escape_hatch: the app's own encryption over kv or a granted file

boundaries.standardizes: the invite-code boundary: a bucket is shared only with the machines that hold its code
boundaries.application_choice: whether to sync at all, what is shared, or the app's own backend over the network boundary
boundaries.escape_hatch: http-client or ws to a service the developer runs

boundaries.standardizes: that a group's data is reachable only by apps whose signed publisher names them in the group's list, and that a removal is not undone by an older list
boundaries.application_choice: whether to share at all, what is shared, and which of the publisher's apps belong
boundaries.escape_hatch: shared under an invite code, or http-client or ws to a service the developer runs

boundaries.standardizes: that an organisation's app data is reachable only from that organisation's marked, signed, released and not withdrawn app, by a member inside the release's audience; that it is sealed on members' devices under the organisation keyring so the hub stores ciphertext only; that edits merge per field by a hybrid logical clock the hub and the device apply identically; and that the people it names to the app are only the release's audience, by sign-in name and role
boundaries.application_choice: whether to keep team data at all, its collections, records and fields, when to sync, or the app's own backend over the network boundary
boundaries.escape_hatch: http-client or ws to a service the organisation runs

boundaries.standardizes: where the host clock is read
boundaries.application_choice: everything computed from it
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed

boundaries.standardizes: a blocking sleep for CLI apps
boundaries.application_choice: scheduling, timers, event loops built on it or not
boundaries.escape_hatch: events/wait with a timeout in GUI apps

boundaries.standardizes: widget kinds, event shapes and errors every host lowers to
boundaries.application_choice: what the app builds from them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: a type carries no authority

boundaries.standardizes: that windows come from the host and are closed by the person
boundaries.application_choice: how many, what size, what is drawn in them
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: a window is the host's

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: an optional portable widget tree the hosts lower to native controls or paint
boundaries.application_choice: any UI approach; a canvas of the app's own pixels is equal to a tree
boundaries.escape_hatch: image and canvas widgets with the app's own rendering

boundaries.standardizes: that input arrives from the host, one event at a time, in the person's own order
boundaries.application_choice: what every event means
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: input is the host's to deliver

boundaries.standardizes: that the person can always take a held pointer back: Escape and focus loss release it on every system
boundaries.application_choice: what the pointer does: aiming, turning a camera, dragging, menus
boundaries.escape_hatch: the mouse's own motion, unfiltered, while the pointer is held

boundaries.standardizes: every finger on a touch screen, by a stable id, in logical pixels, cleared when the window loses focus
boundaries.application_choice: what each finger does: a stick, a look, a button, a gesture
boundaries.escape_hatch: the raw finger positions, unfiltered

boundaries.standardizes: reminders the system delivers with the app closed -- set by an app's own id, after a delay or daily, cancelled, listed -- each app seeing only its own, a tap opening the app
boundaries.application_choice: what to remind, when, and how often
boundaries.escape_hatch: notify for one shown now

boundaries.standardizes: picking photos through the system's own photo picker, returned as chosen files, and adding a PNG or JPEG to the library behind photos.add with add-only access
boundaries.application_choice: when to pick, how many, and what to add
boundaries.escape_hatch: dialog.open-file and save-file, which already exist

boundaries.standardizes: handing a text, a link and files (name and bytes) to the system's share sheet, and hearing only sent or cancelled
boundaries.application_choice: what to share and when; where it goes is the person's pick
boundaries.escape_hatch: save-file and the clipboard, which already exist

boundaries.standardizes: Bluetooth LE reached only through a device the person picks in Krate's own list, then read, write, subscribe and notifications by service and characteristic UUID
boundaries.application_choice: which service to ask for, what to read and write, and what the values mean
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: bluetooth.connect is opt-in, and an app can never scan or reach a device the person did not pick

boundaries.standardizes: one fix of where the phone is -- latitude, longitude, how far off it may be, altitude, speed and course when known -- and the three reasons there is none
boundaries.application_choice: when to ask, how often, and what to do with the position
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: location.read is opt-in, asked on Krate's sheet and by the phone itself

boundaries.standardizes: one reading of the phone's sensors -- gravity, the push given it, its turning and the compass heading -- in the screen's own frame however the phone is turned
boundaries.application_choice: whether to read, how often, and what tilt or shake means to the app
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: no capability, and a device without sensors answers available() false

boundaries.standardizes: the seven feels a phone taps back with and an impact's strength from 0 to 1, each played as the platform's own
boundaries.application_choice: when to tap and which feel; whether to tap at all
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: no capability, and a device with nothing to tap answers available() false

boundaries.standardizes: how a window's screen is described: its size classes, touch or pointer, and the edges something else covers
boundaries.application_choice: every layout decision; the classes are information, not a layout
boundaries.escape_hatch: canvas-size and the app's own breakpoints

boundaries.standardizes: showing and hiding the system's on-screen keyboard for a window; typing arrives as ordinary text and key events
boundaries.application_choice: when a field wants text, and drawing the field and its caret
boundaries.escape_hatch: the raw text and key events, the same as a physical keyboard's

boundaries.standardizes: keeping a decoded picture in the host for a canvas and drawing it by handle, with the same placement as draw-pixels
boundaries.application_choice: which pictures to keep, when to forget them, where and how big to draw them
boundaries.escape_hatch: draw-pixels, which sends the pixels every call

boundaries.standardizes: playing a bundled or granted-host video with the platform decoder and drawing its current frame into a canvas by handle
boundaries.application_choice: which video, its controls and their look, where and how big to draw it, when to play, pause, seek, loop or mute
boundaries.escape_hatch: decode frames in the app and draw them with draw-pixels

boundaries.standardizes: an OAuth 2 PKCE pair and the system sign-in sheet that returns the address a service sends the person back to
boundaries.application_choice: which service, its client id, scopes and redirect, when to ask, how to trade the code and where to keep the token
boundaries.escape_hatch: open-url to the browser and a code the person pastes back

boundaries.standardizes: asking the system to check it is the device owner (Face ID, Touch ID, the passcode) with the app's reason, answered yes, no or unavailable
boundaries.application_choice: what to guard, when to ask and lock again, the reason shown, and what to do when the device cannot check
boundaries.escape_hatch: the app's own passphrase

boundaries.standardizes: reading whether the system is in dark mode, wants more contrast, and the person's text size
boundaries.application_choice: the colours for light and dark, how text grows, and how the layout makes room for it
boundaries.escape_hatch: the app's own fixed look (check-app fails one that stays bright in dark mode or keeps text small)

boundaries.standardizes: telling the platform screen reader what a self-drawn window shows: frames, roles, labels, values and toggle states, with activation as a tap at the centre
boundaries.application_choice: what each element is called and says, the reading order, and when to describe again
boundaries.escape_hatch: widget apps, which Krate describes itself

boundaries.standardizes: showing an https page in a box of the window in the system web view, every navigation judged against the app's net.connect grants, with no stored data and no script channel to the app
boundaries.application_choice: which page, where and how big, when to go elsewhere, go back or close it
boundaries.escape_hatch: open-url to the browser, or fetching and drawing the content itself

boundaries.standardizes: the pixel handoff: an image widget shows what the app hands it
boundaries.application_choice: any renderer, any format decoded by the app
boundaries.escape_hatch: this is the escape hatch for drawing

boundaries.standardizes: that a path outside the grants is chosen by the person in a system dialog, never named by the app
boundaries.application_choice: when to ask, what to do with the answer
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: this is how the person's authority reaches the app

boundaries.standardizes: that nothing reaches a printer unless the person says so in the system's own dialog, and that the answer is what happened (printed, cancelled, or opened in the viewer), never a guess
boundaries.application_choice: what is on each page, how many pages, and when to offer printing
boundaries.escape_hatch: write a PDF the app built itself to a picked folder, or share it

boundaries.standardizes: that the clipboard is the person's and reached through a grant
boundaries.application_choice: what is put on it
boundaries.escape_hatch: none: the clipboard is the host's
boundaries.gap: wired on Linux only today; other hosts answer unsupported

boundaries.standardizes: nothing yet: menu calls are declared and answer unsupported
boundaries.application_choice: any command scheme drawn in the app
boundaries.escape_hatch: the app's own drawn menus and key handling
boundaries.gap: set-items answers unsupported on every host (IC-745)

boundaries.standardizes: that opening a link goes through the person's browser and is a grant, not a process capability
boundaries.application_choice: which links
boundaries.escape_hatch: show the URL and let the person copy it

boundaries.standardizes: that a notification is attributed to the app the person consented to, never to a title the app chose, and is a grant
boundaries.application_choice: when and what
boundaries.escape_hatch: draw the message in the app's own window

boundaries.standardizes: what an app declares it needs, so the person can be told before it runs; an undeclared call is denied
boundaries.application_choice: everything not declared as a capability: architecture, libraries, data model
boundaries.escape_hatch: declare narrowly; optional capabilities are asked for at feature time (CP2)

boundaries.standardizes: one container every host opens: fixed core entries, namespaces, ceilings, a versioned profile
boundaries.application_choice: what the app is made of; unknown entries survive so a tool may carry its own
boundaries.escape_hatch: unknown entries are ignored by the runtime and kept by the packer

boundaries.standardizes: that the executable is a component of a declared world importing only krate:* interfaces
boundaries.application_choice: the language and toolchain that produced it: anything that emits a valid component is accepted at pack, publish and open
boundaries.escape_hatch: the validator (krate_bundle::judge_bytes) is the whole contract; cargo-component is a default, not a requirement
boundaries.gap: the SDK and Studio build with cargo-component only; a developer's own build tool is accepted by the validator but not by the make flow (IC-175: custom build tool)

boundaries.standardizes: that a signature proves who signed these exact bytes and nothing more, that storage follows verified lineage, and that a fork is visibly a fork
boundaries.application_choice: whether to sign at all: an unsigned app runs, labelled
boundaries.escape_hatch: run unsigned; sign with the developer's own offline key, no account

boundaries.standardizes: admission of what it will host: the same validator the runtime uses, and a takedown record with an appeal
boundaries.application_choice: where to host and distribute: a .krate runs from any URL or file, and the hub is one option
boundaries.escape_hatch: any web host, any file share, a link by hand; the client holds fetched bytes to their address wherever they came from

boundaries.standardizes: nothing about the app: the authoring pack teaches the contract, and check-app measures the result
boundaries.application_choice: the developer edits the source by hand at any point; an AI suggestion, repair or regeneration is a proposal the developer may reject
boundaries.escape_hatch: the bundle carries its source, Cargo.lock and SDK; open it and build without Studio

boundaries.standardizes: nothing: a read-only porting assistant with honest verdicts
boundaries.application_choice: whether to port, what to replace, which dependencies to keep
boundaries.escape_hatch: write the app directly against the SDK

boundaries.id: resource limits and the permission wall
boundaries.standardizes: that an app cannot exceed what the person granted or exhaust the machine: memory, entry counts, archive ceilings, denied undeclared calls
boundaries.application_choice: everything within the grants
boundaries.escape_hatch: declare what is needed; the wall explains every denial in plain words

boundaries.standardizes: that nothing leaves the machine without the person's consent, and what does is anonymous and says why an open failed
boundaries.application_choice: an app's own analytics, over the network boundary, declared
boundaries.escape_hatch: none needed: it is opt-in
